<evidence>
Evidence:
[Evidence 1]
Mapper levels describe experience. Typical deployments use Beginner, Intermediate, and Advanced. Each level has an ordering — a higher level satisfies any lower-level requirement. Projects may set a minimum mapping level or minimum validation level; you must meet or exceed that level to lock a task for the relevant action. - **Who can view levels:** Anyone can view level definitions. - **Who can change levels:** Only administrators can create or edit levels. - **Who can move between levels:** The system updates levels automatically based on your mapping statistics after you complete tasks. Lower levels cannot self-promote arbitrarily. Badges are achievements earned by meeting statistical milestones. They are assigned automatically by the system when your statistics satisfy their requirements. You can view badges assigned to you. How level progression works After you finish mapping or validation, the system checks whether new badges have been earned and whether your level threshold is met. If so, your level advances. On some deployments, level changes may involve an approval or voting step. Restrictions - A project can require Intermediate for validation while allowing Beginner for mapping — the two thresholds are independent. - Your level is checked each time you try to lock a task; being promoted does not retroactively affect locks you already hold. See also - [Roles and permissions — overview] — how level gates are evaluated. - [Validating tasks] Sources - Mapping level and badge models, mapping level and badge services, user service, and profile views.
Note: this passage carries a needs-verification caveat — treat thresholds/durations as provisional.

[Evidence 2]
Reading the project page and selecting a task How do I understand the project page? The project page is organized into sections: - **Description** — Why the project exists and what area it covers. - **Instructions** — Exactly what to map, tagging guidance, what imagery to use, and the changeset comment to include. - **Priority areas** — Highlighted polygons that indicate higher-priority zones within the overall area. - **Activity** — Recent history of state changes on tasks. - **Statistics** — Progress bars for mapped and validated percentages, plus totals. Tip: Read the instructions fully, including the per-task notes if the project provides them, before selecting a task. How do I select a task? On the Contribute tab you can either: - **Pick a task on the map** — Click a task square to select it, or - **Take a random task** — Let the system choose one for you. If the project enforces random selection, you must use the random option and cannot choose freely. Task grid Tasks are shown as a grid colored by state. A legend explains the colors for Ready, Mapped, Validated, and other states. Priority areas appear as a distinct overlay. You can filter or search tasks within the project by state. For the meaning of each color and state, see [Task states and lifecycle]. Prerequisites - The project must be published and visible to you. Private or draft projects may be hidden. See [Private projects and access control]. - You must meet any level, team, or license requirements the project sets. See [Roles and permissions — overview]. Permissions — who can select and who cannot - **Who can:** Mappers who are permitted to map on that project. The checks include project published, license accepted if required, mapper level satisfied, team membership if required, private allowed-list if applicable, and no other lock held. - **Who cannot:** Guests cannot select for mapping; mappers who already have a task locked cannot select another; mappers below the required level or not in a required team cannot select; mappers not on the allowed list for a private project cannot select. When blocked, the interface shows a permission reason or you receive an error with a as `UserAlreadyHasTaskLocked`, `PrivateProject`, `ProjectNotPublished`, or `UserNotAcceptedLicense`. See [Error codes and troubleshooting].
Note: this passage carries a needs-verification caveat — treat thresholds/durations as provisional.

[Evidence 3]
Who can map A mapper can lock a task for mapping when **all** of these are true: 1. They are not blocked and are logged in. 2. The project is published. 3. They have no other task currently locked (mapping and validation share a single lock budget — see [One-lock rule]( #one-lock-rule)). 4. Any required data license for the project has been accepted. 5. Their mapper level meets the project's minimum mapping level, if one is set. 6. If the project restricts mapping to teams, they belong to a team assigned as Mappers (or Validators or Project Managers) for that project. 7. If the project is private, they are on the allowed list or in an assigned team, or they are an organization manager or administrator. Who cannot: guests cannot map; blocked users cannot map; users who have not accepted a required license cannot map; users below the required level cannot map; users not in a required team cannot map; users not on the allowed list for a private project cannot map; users who already have a task locked cannot lock another. Each failure returns a distinct error such as `UserNotAllowed`, `ProjectNotPublished`, `UserAlreadyHasTaskLocked`, or `UserNotAcceptedLicense`. If the task is not in a mappable state (for example it is already validated), the error is `InvalidTaskState`. Who can validate Validation follows a similar decision but checks validation-specific gates: 1. The mapper is not blocked and is logged in. 2. The project is published. 3. They have no other task locked (mapping and validation share a single lock budget — see [One-lock rule]( #one-lock-rule)). 4. Required license accepted. 5. Their mapper level meets the project's minimum validation level (often Intermediate by default). 6. If validation is restricted to teams, they belong to a team assigned as Validators or Project Managers for that project. A team assigned only as Mappers is not sufficient. 7. Private project allowed-list/team check as above. Additionally, validators **cannot validate their own mapping** unless they are an administrator — only administrators may validate their own tasks. Project managers, organization managers, and other validators cannot self-validate, even though they can validate tasks mapped by other users. Attempting to self-validate without administrator permission returns `CannotValidateMappedTask`. The distinction is: being able to *validate tasks* on a project (level/team/license) does not grant the ability to validate *your own* task. The task must be in Mapped, Bad imagery, or Invalidated to be locked for validation; otherwise the error is `NotReadyForValidation`.

[Evidence 4]
Do I need prior mapping knowledge to participate? No — the Mapper Guide implies beginners can start with **beginner** projects by following the project instructions. No prior knowledge is required for those; intermediate and advanced projects are reserved for more experienced mappers.

[Evidence 5]

If the project says mapping is team-restricted but no mapper team is assigned, the project cannot be saved. - **Level-gated** compares your mapper level ordering to the project's required level. Being below the threshold blocks lock with `UserNotCorrectMappingLevel`. Levels are described in [Mapper levels and badges]. Organization and project-manager bypass Project author, organization managers, assigned team managers with the Project Manager role for that project, and administrators are treated as managers for that project and bypass team, level, and private-list checks when viewing or managing the project. What happens if you try All permission failures return a JSON error with a stable `SubCode` and a 403 or 409 status. See [Error codes and troubleshooting] to translate a what went wrong and what to do next. Editors and imagery Which editors can I use? The project specifies which editors are allowed. Extra editor parameters configured for the project are passed through. Each project may specify custom imagery — often a TMS URL or template — or fall back to a default such as Bing. - **Background selection:** Choose the suggested custom imagery or a standard source in the editor. - **Imagery offset:** Some projects include an offset to align imagery with existing OSM data. The offset is applied when you open the editor and cleared when no offset is configured. - **Fallbacks:** If imagery is empty, the preset list is missing, or a task download fails, the editor falls back silently: background may switch to the default, offset is reset, preset filters are cleared, or a subtle log is recorded. This is not a hard error — check the imagery menu on the task. Presets Projects may limit which presets (feature templates) are available in iD via preset allow-lists. If the preset configuration is missing or malformed, presets reset to the full set. GPX overlay Some tasks offer a GPX file of the task boundary to side-load into your editor for guidance. Malformed lists are ignored and fall back to the full set. - **Editors:** Choose which editors are allowed for mapping and for validation (iD, JOSM, Potlatch, Field Papers, Custom, Rapid). At least one must be allowed for each, and a custom editor URL is required if Custom is selected. - **Rapid and custom editor:** Manage name, URL, and description for a custom editor such as Rapid. Attempts return a permission error.
